question: What does the idiom 'Jack up the rates' mean?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "Increase prices".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Jack up the rates"** means to raise or increase prices (कीमतें बढ़ाना).
 
 
• **Example:** The shopkeeper decided to jack up the rates of essential commodities during the festival season.
 
 
• **"Increase prices"** refers to raising the cost of goods or services. (मूल्य बढ़ाना)
 
 
• **Example:** The company announced that it would increase prices of its products due to rising raw material costs.
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "Jack up the rates" directly corresponds to the meaning of "Increase prices".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "Increase prices".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: Drop prices** (कीमतें घटाना): To reduce the cost of goods or services.
 
 
• **Example:** The store decided to drop prices to attract more customers during the sale.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: Stay unchanged** (जैसा है वैसा ही रहना): Refers to not making any changes in the existing prices or rates.
 
 
• **Example:** Despite the market fluctuations, the company decided to keep the rates unchanged.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: Sell everything** (सभी कुछ बेचना): Refers to the act of selling all available products or stock.
 
 
• **Example:** The vendor managed to sell everything by the end of the day.
 
 

171:Tb2e,
The correct answer is **Option 4**.</spa
